result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with multiple travel lanes and standard marked crosswalks. While pedestrian signals and sidewalks are present, the long crossing distance and lack of physical protection like medians increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic in a car-centric environment.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the center of the image

hazards.name: Low-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The standard dashed line markings are less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility continental patterns.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade standard transverse markings to continental or ladder patterns to increase visibility to motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban arterial with multiple travel lanes and a significant crossing distance for pedestrians. While sidewalks and green-painted conflict zone markings are present, the lack of a median refuge and the overall scale of the roadway prioritize vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: High Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide, straight lanes and lack of vertical traffic calming elements encourage higher vehicle speeds in an area with residential land use.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes stretching into the background

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unsignalized crossing beneath a dark highway underpass. While a high-visibility marked crosswalk exists, the lack of pedestrian signals, poor lighting under the structure, and narrow sidewalks create a hostile environment for walking.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility under Bridge
hazards.description: Deep shadows under the bridge structure significantly reduce the visibility of pedestrians to oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center area under the bridge structure

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Multi-lane Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without the protection of a signal, stop sign, or refuge island.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk on the left block sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Enhanced Underpass Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity, pedestrian-scale lighting under the bridge to eliminate dark spots and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Activated Warning System
interventions.description: Install Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB) to alert drivers when a pedestrian is attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting the Crosswalk
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment is a wide, multi-lane one-way arterial road designed for high vehicle throughput, featuring overhead highway-style signage. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crosswalks and signals are present, the scale of the roadway creates a long, exposed crossing for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic in a single stage, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crossing across the main roadway

hazards.name: High-speed road geometry
hazards.description: Wide lanes and overhead highway signage encourage higher vehicle speeds in an urban context.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes and overhead gantry

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, increasing visibility.
